clue.text: Material to fire churchmen

parts.note: to fire someone from a job is to sack them
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Fabric used for dismissing clergymen, as if a bishop were firing his priests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is an old collective name for the clergy, from their distinctive dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Sackcloth is a coarse fabric, traditionally worn in mourning or penitence.

clue.text: Hardened fellow causing deadlock

parts.note: stale bread has hardened
a mate is a fellow or companion

explanation.surface: A tough man is responsible for the impasse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardened' suggests a tough character but means gone stale like old bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalemate is a chess position with no legal move, and by extension any impasse.

clue.text: Having caught a fish, hold on

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler who has hooked a fish is told to keep a grip.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scorecards C stands for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grip tightly and not let go.

clue.text: "Good wine is a good familiar ______ if it be well used." (Othello)

definitions.text: Good wine is a good familiar

parts.note: the solver fills the gap in Iago's line from Othello praising wine as a friendly living thing

explanation.surface: A quotation from Othello with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: Iago says 'Good wine is a good familiar creature, if it be well used' in Act 2 of Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago calls wine a friendly living being, using the word for any animal or person.

clue.text: A doubter can be difficult to influence

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters can be made into another word

explanation.surface: A sceptic may be hard to persuade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges the letters of A DOUBTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubborn, refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Poles following a brave man in waders

indicators.note: following puts the poles behind the brave man in the answer

parts.note: a hero is a brave man
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people trail behind a courageous man wearing fishing boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people but means the north and south poles; 'waders' looks like boots but means wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons are long-legged wading birds that stalk fish in shallow water.

clue.text: Sprays of flowers

explanation.surface: A florist's description of bouquets.
explanation.walkthrough: A rose is also the perforated nozzle of a watering can that breaks water into a spray.
explanation.definitionFit: Watering-can nozzles that make sprays share the name with the familiar thorny garden blooms.

clue.text: A writer taking baby-food home

parts.note: a rusk is a hard biscuit given to teething babies
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: An author carries his child's food back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: A rusk is a hard dry biscuit common as British baby food.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin was a Victorian art critic and essayist.

clue.text: Give voice about transport taxing

indicators.note: about means around, so the singing word goes round the transport word

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Complaining aloud about a levy on travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxing' looks like levying tax but means demanding effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining work is tiring and demanding, pushing one to the limit.

clue.text: Not smiling back

explanation.surface: A sombre expression in return.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the rear part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe, unsmiling face is stern, and the rear of a boat is also called its stern.

clue.text: One's restricted by a lack of distinctive taste

indicators.note: something restricted by other letters is hemmed in by them, so it goes inside

parts.note: a lack or want is a need
one is I, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A person feels limited by having no distinctive flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is a contraction: the I of 'one' plus the 's that stands for 'is'; 'restricted by' then hems those letters inside a phrase meaning a lack.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant gives a strong liquorice flavour used in sweets and drinks.

clue.text: About to be a soldier in the TA

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
soldiers serve in the army, so to be a soldier is to serve

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of joining up as a part-time soldier in the Territorial Army.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's force of part-time volunteer soldiers kept back to support the regular army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Territorial Army is the British Army's volunteer standby force, held back for when it is needed.

clue.text: A number may well get involved in a row

definitions.text: may well get involved in a row

explanation.surface: A figure that seems likely to end up in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means rowing: an eight is a racing boat with eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the numeral after seven, and also a rowing crew of that many oarsmen.

clue.text: Ride in — not to make a delivery

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declines to ride in to drop off a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' turns the letters of RIDE IN and NOT into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance, the way a song or speech is delivered.

clue.text: Bill presented by a minister? That's right

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a curate is a junior minister of the Church

explanation.surface: A churchman hands over the bill and asks whether that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' is a clergyman here, not a government member.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and right both mean correct, free from error.

clue.text: Figure maybe he's an outstanding individual

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain person may be remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: A figure such as a digit is a character in printing; a character is also a distinctive, eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Written symbols such as numerals are characters, and a memorable eccentric is called a character.

clue.text: This association of interested people is sound

explanation.surface: A claim that a group of enthusiasts is solid and reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable; it is the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a cartel or clique pursuing shared ends, and to ring is to make a bell sound.

clue.text: Inexperienced band with no opportunities for development

parts.note: green means new and inexperienced
a belt is a band or strip

explanation.surface: A new pop group finds no chance of growing.
explanation.walkthrough: A green belt is a ring of countryside around a British town where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning law protects such open land round cities from being built upon.

clue.text: Sweets must be given up, it's emphasised

indicators.note: in a down clue, given up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: desserts are sweet courses, called sweets in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that sugary food must be abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' looks like abandoning but means written upwards, turning DESSERTS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressed syllable is one given emphasis.

clue.text: Many a canary is a seasonal singer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a roller is a breed of canary known for its rolling song

explanation.surface: Lots of canaries sing at a particular time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: The roller is a canary bred for song; C, a hundred, stands for many.
explanation.definitionFit: A caroller sings Christmas songs door to door.

clue.text: Key to a hold-up in the Netherlands

parts.note: E is a musical key
a dam holds up a river's water

explanation.surface: The secret of a robbery somewhere in Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' suggests a robbery but means a barrier holding up water.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a town in North Holland, famous for its round cheese.

clue.text: Put an end to alien pocketing the money

indicators.note: something that pockets other letters takes them inside itself

parts.note: alien and strange both mean foreign or unfamiliar
L stands for the pound, Britain's money, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Stop a foreigner from stealing the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts L inside STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle something, such as a plan, is to choke it off and stop it.

clue.text: Murmur an egghead can appear benevolent

parts.note: to hum is to murmur
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A muttering intellectual may seem kindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means kind and compassionate.

clue.text: Fret as change is increasingly accelerated

indicators.note: change tells us these letters change order

explanation.surface: Worry grows as alteration speeds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges FRET AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Faster is the comparative of fast, meaning more quickly.

clue.text: Cake catalogue (fancy)

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, telling us the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of elaborate gateaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cake' is a verb, to harden into a crust or clot.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood or mud that cakes clots and thickens into a solid mass.

clue.text: Swear nothing has left the road

indicators.note: something that has left is gone, so it is removed

parts.note: a course is a route or road taken
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone cursing as their car leaves the road with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: O, nothing, leaves COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language.

clue.text: Frequently expressed as decimal

explanation.surface: A remark that something is often written as a decimal number.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: something decimal is based on the number after nine, which written out as a phrase is 'of' plus that number, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means many times over, and split in two it describes counting in tens.

clue.text: Taking heart, a Briton gained these islands

indicators.note: the heart is the inside, so the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: Encouraged, an Englishman acquired an archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking heart' looks like being encouraged but tells the solver to take letters from the middle of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific kingdom made up of many islands.

clue.text: Withdraw pamphlet after note

indicators.note: after places the pamphlet word behind the note in the answer

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: An instruction to pull a leaflet once a memo has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is a musical note from do-re-mi, not a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back.

clue.text: Quiet judge of Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A calm evaluation of the Bard's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Justice Silence is a country magistrate in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2; 'judge' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet is the absence of noise, and Shallow's fellow justice in Henry IV Part 2 bears that name.

clue.text: English soldiers turned back, and that's strange

indicators.note: turned back means the soldiers' letters are read the other way

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: British troops retreated, which seemed odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' makes ER from RE, and 'that's' is read as 'that is', abbreviated IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means uncanny or weird, giving a sense of unease.

clue.text: A bird given bread perhaps among other things

indicators.note: among puts the scrambled bread inside the other word

parts.note: the rest means the others or other things

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A bird gets bread as well as other food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the five letters of the loaf are jumbled, and 'among' places that jumble inside a phrase for other things; 'given' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbreast is a traditional name for the robin.
